newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 3.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- President Kim Young-sam is expected to name a new prime minister soon, possibly in a couple of days, sources said.

- Former National Security Planning Board officer Kim Ki-sup denied passing on information to President Kim Young-sam's second son, Kim Hyun-chul. He did admit to being close friends with Kim, saying they met socially at least once a month.
- Koh Kun, president of Myunggi University is highly likely to be named as the new prime minister, inside sources said.
